title: Multi-region circuit hysteresis tuning and traffic smoothing (SLO drift follow-up)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up work for the 2026-01-17 cross-region SLO drift where automated failover plus circuit breaker hysteresis caused cascading reroutes and sustained tail-latency degradation. This ticket captures the root cause summary, immediate mitigations applied, and a prioritized set of long-term changes (tuning, observability, and control-plane safeguards) to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-01-17 03:12 UTC: Region us-west-2 reported 99th percentile latency spike for generation endpoints; automated region failover triggered
2026-01-17 03:15 UTC: Circuit breaker policy in central control-plane evaluated region health and began aggressive cross-region reroutes to us-east-1
2026-01-17 03:18 UTC: us-east-1 hit CPU/GPU saturation for several model shards; KV cache warmup increased cache-miss ratio and token tail latencies rose
2026-01-17 03:25 UTC: Circuit hysteresis parameters caused the system to keep failing back-and-forth between regions for ~12 minutes
2026-01-17 03:40 UTC: On-call applied temporary manual damping: increase hysteresis window, reduce cross-region fanout threshold, and enable per-model capacity caps
2026-01-17 04:05 UTC: Latencies stabilized and SLOs recovered to acceptable range; incident closed for immediate remediation
impact_summary: Customers in EU and NA experienced elevated tail latency (95th and 99th percentile) for ~30 minutes, causing ~4% of requests to miss the 300ms SLO and some downstream retries. No data loss or leaked customer data. Estimated customer-visible error budget burn: medium-high for affected customers.
root_cause: A combination of overly-aggressive automated failover policy and conservative circuit-breaker hysteresis settings led to oscillatory cross-region traffic. The control-plane decision logic lacked short-term capacity awareness (per-shard GPU utilization and cache warmup costs) and treated route health as binary rather than a graded score. This caused capacity amplification when failovers redirected traffic into already-healthy-but-near-capacity regions, which then tripped local overload protections and propagated further reroutes.
contributing_factors: Circuit breaker hysteresis window too short and symmetric for two-region topologies
Control-plane health scoring failed to weigh transient cache warmup costs and KV miss amplification
No per-model or per-shard immediate capacity reservation during failover (no soft pre-warm)
Alert thresholds were primarily rate-based and did not surface tail-latency pattern early enough
Runbook lacked explicit guidance for damping oscillatory reroutes
immediate_mitigations: Manual increase of circuit hysteresis window from 30s to 180s during incident
Temporarily capped cross-region fanout to 1.5x normal peak traffic per region
Enabled per-model throughput caps on busiest model variants to allow graceful degradation instead of hard failover
Added short-duration KV-cache pre-warm hook for failover paths in control plane codebase (hotfix PR linked below)
long_term_actions: Tune circuit-breaker hysteresis to be asymmetric and proportional to recent capacity margin (design + implementation) — owner: Marco Nguyen — ETA 2026-02-12
Add graded health scoring in control plane that factors in per-shard GPU utilization, KV warmup penalty, and recent tail-latency trend — owner: Claire Thompson — ETA 2026-03-01

Implement predictive pre-warm: when control plane schedules a planned failover or large reroute, proactively pre-warm KV caches and reserve soft slots for top N models — owner: SRE team lead (Ravi Patel) — ETA 2026-04-01
Create an automated damping layer that prevents oscillatory reroutes by applying exponential backoff per-route and hysteresis amplification after a failback — owner: Runtime infra — ETA 2026-02-26
Improve alerting to include tail-latency slope anomalies and warmup-loss signals, add targeted dashboards for cross-region reroute patterns — owner: Observability — ETA 2026-02-05
Update runbooks with explicit steps for damping, temporary capacity caps, and decision criteria for manual rollback — owner: On-call lead — ETA 2026-02-02
Schedule a chaos test that simulates region degradation with induced KV-cache cold starts to validate damping policies — owner: Reliability eng — ETA 2026-03-15
notes: Trade-offs discussed: larger hysteresis reduces sensitivity to real regional failures; mitigated by graded health scoring to reintroduce sensitivity when capacity margin exists
We intentionally did not fully disable automated failover because the risk of single-region prolonged outage is higher; preferred approach is smarter routing instead of turning features off
This incident reveals an observability gap: we lacked an easy signal for 'cache-warmup penalty' which is now being instrumented
Estimate for full implementation across control-plane and runtime ~8-10 SRE/eng sprint-weeks due to testing and chaos validation needs
